rationale: STRK-282: v2 tab shell — the four visibility panels (Dashboard/Inventory/Market/Collections) wrapping the existing page sections, driven by the header nav and the mobile bottom bar. Covers: boot state (Dashboard active, other three hidden, aria-selected on the right button); switching panels via the header nav and the aria-selected handoff; and section-to-panel membership for all six wrapped sections. THE REAL RISK THIS FILE GUARDS IS NOT SWITCHING — it is code that reaches across sections by DOM POSITION, which the wrappers silently break. Two such bugs were found landing this and are pinned here as named regression guards: (1) applyLayoutOrder (js/settings.js) re-appended every section to `.container` to reassert DOM order, and running at boot from init.js it EJECTED all six sections out of the panels — the wrappers collapsed to zero height and every section rendered on every tab. Deceptive symptom: the page still looks fully populated because the sections are all present, just no longer tabbed, and the whole Playwright suite passed green against that broken state because nothing was hidden. Sections now append into the owning view via LAYOUT_SECTION_TAB_VIEW. (2) showInventoryRecoveryBanner (js/inventory.js) mounted via tableSection.parentNode.insertBefore — that parent used to be <main>, so wrapping #tableSectionEl moved the mount INSIDE a display:none panel and a user with unreadable inventory would land on Dashboard and never see the data-loss warning; it now mounts above the panels and the test asserts it survives a tab switch. NOTE for anyone adding specs that touch inventory: #newItemBtn lives in the Inventory panel, so a bare goto(/index.html) leaves it display:none — deep-link goto(/index.html#/inventory), which is why ten core specs carry that hash. SECOND DESCRIBE BLOCK — STRK-326: whole-tab visibility. Under the old flat 'Visible sections' list, unticking the single section a tab owned emptied that tab but LEFT ITS NAV ENTRY IN PLACE, so users got a live link to a blank panel. Tab visibility is now derived from the sections a tab owns (LAYOUT_SECTION_TAB_VIEW is the single source of truth for both this and applyLayoutOrder) and no second localStorage key was added. Covers: nav entries dropped on BOTH surfaces; deep link to a hidden tab falling back to Dashboard; Dashboard locked visible so a fallback target always exists; hiding the ACTIVE tab re-homing the user and rewriting the hash; the Inventory checkbox writing both sections it owns (search + table render as one surface); arrow keys skipping hidden tabs; and the split Settings tables (four tab rows with no arrows, Dashboard-only section rows). TWO TRAPS PINNED HERE: (1) the mobile bar's .bottom-nav-btn declares display:flex, which OUTRANKS the user-agent [hidden] rule — without the css/styles.css `[hidden] { display: none !important }` override the attribute sets correctly and nothing moves on screen, a failure invisible to any test asserting on the attribute rather than on toBeHidden(). (2) 'Dashboard cannot be hidden' asserts .active + aria-selected, NOT toBeVisible(): with every section display:none the panel collapses to a zero-size box, so a visibility assertion on the wrapper tests its children, not reachability. (3) THE FALLBACK MUST CORRECT THE HASH. The boot deep-link and the hashchange handler both call activateTab with updateHash=false, so the first cut of the fallback rendered Dashboard while the address bar kept '#/market' — the visible panel and any re-shared or bookmarked link disagreed indefinitely. Caught in review by two independent bots, NOT by the original test, which asserted only the panel. activateTab now corrects a fallen-back tab route with history.replaceState (not assignment: no extra history entry, no re-fired hashchange), guarded on tabFromHash() so a hashless index.html stays hashless. Both the deep-link and hashchange cases now assert the URL, and the hashchange case asserts that ONE Back step returns to the prior tab, which is what distinguishes replaceState from pushState.

STRK-291 adds 10 for the per-card refresh icon freshness colour, kept in this file rather than a new one because it is the same spot-sync domain and AGENTS.md discourages new issue-prefixed spec files. Those 8: three age buckets (fresh <60min / stale <24h / expired beyond); no-timestamps reads stale NOT expired, preserving the pre-existing rule that an empty install must not open on red; a cached entry inside its provider cache duration reads fresh DESPITE a 2h age, which is the only test that catches a dropped getCacheDurationMs fallback chain — it must use a keyed provider because getCacheDurationMs("STAKTRAKR") returns 0 by design so that branch is unreachable for the default source; a successful sync flips expired→fresh, pinning the post-sync hook in updateLastTimestamps; the freshness class coexists with .syncing and .spot-sync-icon, guarding the className= clobber the retired #headerSyncDot body used; and all three states resolve to distinct computed colours in every one of the four themes, which is what catches --warning at ~1.4:1 on --bg-secondary in light and sepia. RACE, cost one full green-then-red cycle: init.js runs the indicator at Phase 12 but fires fetchSpotPrice() at Phase 13, and under the default mock that fetch succeeds ~40ms after DOMContentLoaded and writes wall-clock lastApiSync once per metal, so any pre-boot seed is overwritten and every state collapses to fresh. Waiting on #spotPriceDisplaySilver is NOT sufficient — it is visible long before the fetch resolves. installBootSyncProbe counts writes to the two freshness keys and gotoAppSettled waits for quiescence. The failure is asymmetric and therefore deceptive: overwriting a fresh seed with a fresh value is invisible, so only the expired cases went red while stale passed on timing luck. Do not remove the settle step because the tests appear to pass without it. PR #1410 REVIEW added 2 more and reordered the production logic. Codex and Codacy both spotted that updateLastTimestamps writes BOTH lastApiSync AND lastCacheRefresh on every successful API sync, so the original lastApiSync-first resolution returned before the cache window was ever consulted — a keyed provider with a 24h cache read stale at 90 minutes while the app still considered the data valid and would not refetch, making the entire cache branch unreachable in the field. The pre-existing cache test passed only because it DELETES lastApiSync, a state no real user is ever in; that is precisely how a test can be green and the feature still wrong. The cache-window check now runs first, and "the cache window still wins when a real sync also wrote lastApiSync" seeds both keys the way production does — verified to fail against the pre-review js/spot.js. Its sibling "a cache window that has closed falls back to plain age" guards the over-correction, since putting the cache first could otherwise pin everything to fresh; it uses STAKTRAKR, whose 0 ms window is always closed, and passes both before and after. TWO TRAPS: (1) fetchApiHealth appends a `?_t=` cache buster, so exact-string page.route patterns silently never match — every route needs a `*` suffix, unlike the strk-189 spot-sync routes which hit _staktrakrFetch (no buster); (2) endpoint selection is PER FEED and mirrors two different gates — spot uses the lenient max(stale_after x 6, 2h) regime from _checkSpotEnvelopeFreshness, market mirrors the strict retail regime (the envelope's own stale_after) because the per-slug retail fetches are what deliver on-screen market prices; a single shared rule or a take-the-freshest rule would let the badge claim ages the renderer never shows. STRK-333: freshest-wins must not cost metal coverage. New describe block. The publisher builds spot/latest.json from whichever current rows exist and SKIPS absent metals (devops/pollers/shared/api-export-v2.js exportSpot), bailing only when EVERY row is missing — so a fresh, valid, PARTIAL envelope is reachable in production, and ranking purely by generated_at meant the winner could omit a metal a slightly older endpoint carried. TEST 1 (repair, red-verified by reverting js/api.js) pins the backfill: api1 fresh-but-missing-xag, api2 25m older with silver — silver must land from api2. Its second half is the HONESTY assertion and the reason the design is per-metal timestamps rather than a single collapsed one: the backfilled row must carry api2's generated_at, never the fresher winner's, because stamping 25-minute-old silver as 5 minutes old is the badge-disagrees-with-data failure STRK-331 was opened to kill. TEST 2 is the no-downgrade guard (passes pre-fix by design): when BOTH endpoints carry silver the winner still wins and the runner-up price must never appear, so the fill can only ever reach metals the winner OMITS. NOTE ON THE DESIGN THE CODE FORCED: generatedAt stays the WINNER's because _lastAcceptedSpotGeneratedAtMs rejects any payload older than the last accepted one — reporting the oldest contributing envelope instead would let a backfill trip that monotonic guard and discard the whole sync, fresh metals included. TEST 3 (review round 1, red-verified by deleting the guard line) closes the hole CodeRabbit and Copilot both found independently: an UNDATED runner-up is ungated, not merely undated — _checkEnvelopeFreshness returns ok for any envelope it cannot date, so a legacy or corrupted payload clears STRK-189 without being vouched for, and having no timestamp of its own it fell through to the override-free path and got stamped with the winner's FRESH time. Exactly the overstatement priceTimestamps exists to prevent, and worse than leaving the metal alone. An undated candidate can now only donate when the winner is undated too (all-legacy, generatedAt null, no claim made). The test asserts the invariant independent of sync outcome: the unvouched price reaches neither the display nor the history series. TEST 4 (review round 2, Codex P1, red-verified) moves EVERY spot price onto its own observation time: exportSpot() selects the latest sqld row with NO age cutoff and emits that row's `t` (a 15-minute floor) beside the price, so clearing the envelope gate never proved the PRICE was equally fresh and a just-published envelope could carry an old reading into history as newly minted. Verified against production 2026-08-11: generated_at 00:38:05 with the xag entry at t=00:30:00Z. Applied to winner and runner-up alike rather than only to backfilled metals, because the gap was never specific to backfills and a split rule is harder to reason about than either rule applied uniformly. THE DEDUP INTERACTION IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE FEARED ONE and is why this was safe to land here: recordSpot dedups on timestamp+metal whenever an explicit timestamp is passed (js/spot.js:407), so flooring COLLAPSES repeated syncs inside one 15-minute window onto a single row instead of appending one per publish cycle for a reading that never changed. Existing fixtures carry no `t` and fall back to generated_at, so every prior assertion in this file is untouched.

STRK-332: a fresh manifest does not promise a complete export. exportRetail() catches and skips individual slug failures yet main() still writes a fresh manifest, so the newest-manifest endpoint can be missing slug files; _syncRetailV2 fetched every slug exclusively from that one base and a gap degraded straight to the stored price. Runners-up from the manifest race are now retained and retried per FILE. Red-verified by reverting js/retail.js. THE EXPOSURE PRE-DATES freshest-wins — the old first-HTTP-OK selection was equally single-base, STRK-331 only changed which endpoint can be chosen. TWO TRAPS PINNED HERE: (1) the assertions MUST poll, not snapshot — syncRetailPrices has an in-progress guard so the explicit page.evaluate call can no-op against the boot sync and return before any slug is fetched; a snapshot assertion failed 5 runs in 5 while the sync was demonstrably working, and the api2 gap request is the correct thing to await because it is issued only after api1's 503 for that same file resolves, by which point the Promise.all has already issued every api1 slug request. (2) the scoping assertion cannot demand api2 receive EXACTLY one retail path: this fixture's deliberately unresolvable synthetic slugs (core-unknown-metal-retail-slug) are absent from BOTH endpoints, so all five of their files are legitimately retried on api2 and then given up on — that doubled request count for genuinely-missing files is the cost a fallback is supposed to pay. The meaningful claim, and what the test asserts, is that a file api1 served SUCCESSFULLY is never re-fetched from api2. TEST 2 (review round 2, Codex P1, red-verified) adds the per-file freshness gate the sync never had: reachability only proved an HTTP-successful MANIFEST, so an arbitrarily old slug file could supply the displayed price while _syncRetailV2 stored the winner's fresh manifest timestamp and painted the market freshness dot green — the STRK-331 defect class reached by a different route. _isV2SlugEnvelopeFresh applies the strict regime (the envelope's own stale_after, no multiplier, no slack) inside _fetchV2Json so it covers the PRIMARY and the fallback alike, since the primary was equally ungated. A stale payload returns null, deliberately reusing the missing-file path so the caller escalates to the next base and a slug stale everywhere keeps its stored price rather than showing an unvouched one. THE TEST SHAPE THAT MATTERS IS A STALE 200, not a 503: the 503 case was already covered by TEST 1, and a stale 200 is indistinguishable from a good response without the gate. TWO ESCAPES ARE DELIBERATE and are what keep this file's other 40+ tests alive: an envelope with no parseable generated_at, and one declaring no positive stale_after, both pass — the fixtures emit exactly that shape (generated_at GENERATED_AT, no stale_after) six hours behind the pinned FIXED_NOW clock, so a fail-closed gate would have rejected every fixture in the suite. Budget validated against production 2026-08-11 across 3 slugs x 5 files: every file is rewritten each publish cycle and the worst observed age was 40% of budget (intraday, 1200s), roughly 2.5x headroom before the gate rejects anything real.

STRK-338: js/market-data.js and js/retail.js both own retailManifestCoinMeta and retailManifestVendorMeta and DISAGREED on storage convention. market-data.js writes them through saveDataSync (:294,:306), which wraps anything over 4096 chars in a CMP2: envelope; js/retail.js read them back with a bare getItem + JSON.parse, so a compressed value threw, the catch evicted the key, and the cache silently never restored — market-data then re-fetched and re-compressed it, retail cleared it again, every page load, with the slug list falling back to the 12-item hardcoded RETAIL_SLUGS. THE ISSUE FILED THIS AS LATENT ("would break IF someone later migrated the write"); it is not — the migrating writer already shipped in the other module, and a third one exists at js/vault.js:247, which runs __compressIfNeeded over every ALLOWED_STORAGE_KEYS value on backup restore. ONLY PAYLOAD SIZE HELD IT SHUT: measured against the live manifest on 2026-08-13 (26 coins, 8 vendors) coin meta was 2327 chars against the 4096 threshold and grows ~90 chars/coin, so it crosses at roughly 46 coins — reachable within the planned roster growth, and the break would then surface far from the change that caused it. Fix routes retail.js through loadDataSync/saveDataSync on BOTH sides and collapses the duplicated restore block in initRetailPrices into _restoreRetailManifestCacheFromStorage (the copy-paste twin is how the two halves drifted). THESE TWO TESTS ARE INTEGRATION COVERAGE THE UNIT SUITE CANNOT GIVE: tests/unit/strk-338-manifest-cache-compression.test.js exercises the sliced restore helper against the real codec and real lz-string, but only a page load proves the real WRITER and the real READER agree with both modules present. Red-verified by restoring origin/dev's js/retail.js: the key is absent from localStorage after reload. THE FIXTURE MUST BE OFFLINE — the first draft left the network live, a background manifest sync overwrote the 60-coin fixture with the real 26-coin roster, and the assertion measured the feed instead of the cache; every external request is now aborted so the cache is the only possible source. The CMP2: prefix is asserted before the reload for the same reason the size was measured: if the fixture ever drops under the threshold the test asserts nothing about compression at all.
